parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Summarise the arguments in favour of wearing school uniform raised by members of the
audience.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify and explain four arguments against wearing school uniform raised by members of
the audience.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
In your opinion, explain two advantages and state one disadvantage of a school providing a
uniform for the children to put on at school everyday.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Of the four audience members, explain whose argument you think is the most credible.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Of the four audience members, explain whose argument you think is the least credible.
Section B
Read the material for Section B in the insert before answering the questions in Section B.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify the words or phrases in the material that mean the same as the following phrases:

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
people quickly replace things, once they have broken, with new products, rather than
have them repaired (paragraph 4)

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
plan and make something using guidelines which aim to reduce its impact on the
environment (paragraph 6)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
According to the material, identify two reasons why some people might find a Fairphone
‘liberating’ to use.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Identify and explain four features of a Fairphone that make it more socially and environmentally
sustainable. (lines 9–34)

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Explain the meaning of the following two words as used in the material. You may write your
answers as one word or a short phrase.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Explain three ways in which the company’s office headquarters promotes its environmental
conscience.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text:
Using the material and your own knowledge, suggest why electronic waste is such a problem.
